name: Lush evolving pad from two saws (second −12 st), high unison (~8, shimmer-style detune ~30), long overlapping amp ADSR, a filter envelope that opens from a low start (~200 Hz) with ~2 s attack, plus a slow non-retriggering tempo-synced triangle LFO on cutoff so each chord catches the filter in a different place; optional analog-modelled filter drive and a long low-cut convolution/space
goal: Build a chord pad that feels hand-played rather than looping the same filter shape: stack an octave-down second saw under a unison saw, use long attack/decay/release so chords overlap, open the filter with a second envelope from a dark starting cutoff, then add a very slow triangle LFO with retrigger OFF so successive chords land at different filter positions. Delta vs wavetable cluster: the non-retriggering multi-bar LFO-on-cutoff as the 'alive' mechanism (not wavetable-position morph alone), paired with a dual-octave saw stack and overlapping amp envelope numbers from the source.

source.title: How to Make Lush Evolving Pads in Wavetable | Ableton Tutorial

prerequisites: Wavetable or analog-style synth with ≥2 oscillators, unison, dual envelopes, ≥1 LFO with retrigger on/off and tempo sync, filter with clean/drive models
Reverb or convolution with low-cut; EQ

inputs.name: chords
inputs.description: Wide, multi-octave chord voicings that can overlap

outputs.name: lush_pad
outputs.description: Evolving lush pad with overlapping chord tails

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Steady pitch: the source adds a tiny LFO to pitch for tape drift (~1.5 amount with fade-in); leave it out unless the brief wants wobble.
Prefer filter and wavetable-position motion over pitch motion.
Low-cut the reverb and the pad if a separate bass is present.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.
Steady pitch: leave out intentional pitch-drift LFOs unless the brief asks for tape wobble (Matt prefers steady pitch).

steps.action: Oscillator 1: a saw or near-saw wavetable. Enable unison (classic or shimmer-style) at a high voice count (source uses 8) with detune around 30 — lush and smeared, not out of tune.
Oscillator 2: same saw, pitched −12 semitones, to thicken with a lower octave. Balance levels.
Amp envelope: attack ~2 s; sustain about half the peak (source ~−13 dB on that scale); decay ~6 s; release ~2 s so chord tails overlap instead of stopping dead.

Filter envelope (env 2) → cutoff: start cutoff near ~200 Hz, envelope amount high enough to open clearly (source ~70). Shape env 2 with ~2 s attack and long decay/release so it swells open like the amp, not a pluck.
steps.expect: Pad opens from dark to open

steps.action: LFO 1 → cutoff at moderate depth (source ~40): tempo-sync to a multi-bar rate (source 3 bars or 1.5), triangle shape, and turn retrigger OFF so each new chord catches a different LFO phase — the filter no longer repeats identically every note.

Optional: switch the filter to an analog-modelled / driven mode for mild saturation instead of a separate distortion plugin. Optional: slow LFO or envelope on wavetable position for timbral morph (pitch stays fixed).
Space: a long lush reverb or convolution (source uses a 'black hole'-style IR) with dry/wet raised and a low-cut on the reverb so the pad stays deep without rumble.

verification: Chords overlap via release; no hard stops between changes.
Filter start is dark (~200 Hz) and opens over ~2 s.
With LFO retrigger off, two consecutive chords do not share the same filter trajectory.
No audible pitch wobble in the default patch.
